newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
80 PCT VOTES CAST IN JANATA DAL PARTY POLL

The Janata Dal party's first ever election after its formation in 1988 ended in the Indian capital with supporters of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Yadav boycotting the polls. About 80 percent of the 998 members of the national council of the party cast their votes. But 23 out of its 44 members of the lower house of parliament boycotted the poll. Within hours of the poll Laloo Yadav announced a convention of his supporters on July 5 in New Delhi.
All papers
ECONOMIC COUNCIL TO COORDINATE DEPARTMENTS

The reconstituted Economic Intelligence Council will discuss measures to coordinate the work of law enforcement agencies, monitor important cases involving coordination and keep a watch on economic crimes to suggest effective measures to deal with them.
MUTUAL FUNDS ASKED TO FREEZE NEW SCHEMES

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) asked mutual funds not to launch any new schemes. The SEBI has asked mutual funds to consult with the bourse regulator before opening new schemes. As per existing regulations, mutual funds have only to file the offer document with SEBI after which they receive observations. They are free to launch new schemes 21 days from the day of receiving such observations. The SEBI move is thought to be a fallout of the recent CRB Capital Market scam case.
Financial Express
RESERVE BANK EASES NORMS ON DIVIDEND WARRANTS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) relaxed the 10,000 rupee limit on dividends and warrants issued by companies. It also removed the restrictions on the number of authorised bank branches to service this facility. Banks can now relax these restrictions on a case-to-case basis with each such exemption approved by their board or management committee. This follows complaints by institutions and banks about the difficulties faced by the investors after restrictions were imposed in May this year.
Business Standard
FOREIGN EXCHANGE RULE RELAXED

The Reserve Bank of India relaxed foreign exchange rules by enhancing the bank's power to release foreign exchange. The banks can now remit in advance $15,000 towards import without any bank guarantee. This was $ 5,000 until now. In the case of tie-up arrangements for surface transportation, the banks can now release advance payments up to 10 percent within a limit of $50,000 per tie-up arrangement. They can also release foreign exchange up to $3,000 towards basic travel quota per person and $2,500 for overseas employment per person, $1,000 a year for gifts to friends or relatives abroad, $1,000 for donations abroad and $3,000 for emigration.
STOCKS OPTIONS AT DISCOUNT PLANNED

The government plans to permit companies to offer their shares to employees at about 80 percent of the market value. The bourse regulator (SEBI) is planning discussions on establishing such a concessional price mechanism for employee stock options popularly known as sweet equity. Currently bourse options are offered to employees at the average price of the scrip during the six months preceding an issue. Concessional pricing can be allowed with a rider in the form of a lock-in condition on the shares underlying the stock option. A three year lock-in period is under consideration.
CRACKDOWN ON ERRING EXPORTERS PLANNED

The Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has decided to penalise exporters who are not repatriating their export proceeds. This is to check speculation and to ensure a steady value of the rupee against dollar. The director general had written to all banks seeking information on such exporters. The estimate is that five to seven percent of the exporters are not repatriating their proceeds. Such exporters take duty-free licences and after fulfilling their export commitments fail to bring in money. They get their next set of licence by producing the shipping bills.
TELCO TIES UP WITH FOUR OVERSEAS FIRMS

Tata Engineering and Locomotives Co (TELCO) signed technical agreements with John Deere Industrial Equipment of the United States, Hitachi Construction Machinery and Nachi-Fujikoshi Corporation of Japan, and Le Moteur Moderne of France. The agreement with Hitachi is to make 60-tonne hydraulic excavators, the one with Le Moteur is to develop diesel and petrol engine for cars and the one with Nachi-Fujikoshi is to make an advance generation of robots. The collaboration with John Deere is to make backhoe loaders.
The Observer
BANK EMPLOYEES TO STRIKE WORK FOR A DAY

About 1.3 million bank employees all over India will go on a one-day strike on Friday to protest against a government plan to allow private banks in rural areas. Delhi Banks Employees Federation's assistant secretary said the strike was to protest against the government's decision to allow local area banks in rural areas by the private players and a ban on recruitments and compassionate appointments in government banks. Union leaders said they thought the strike would paralyse banking operations all over the country.
